reasoning: The conversion really is unguarded. GeminiWireTypes.swift:150 takes remaining_fraction unclamped, line 151 clamps only consumedFraction, and line 154 runs Int((rem*100).rounded()), which traps for values beyond Int range. That is a real robustness bug. It does not work as a security finding, because the defenses that matter stop an attacker before this line. (1) The HTTP path: AppConfig.swift:505-527 checks base_url against a fixed Google host list (GeminiConfig.allowedHosts) and falls back to the default when it fails, and the request goes over TLS to generativelanguage.googleapis.com. To inject the payload an attacker would have to be Google, or break TLS or the allowlist. The finding shows no bypass for either. (2) The agy path: AntigravityExecutor.swift:28-45,62-64 runs a local binary from the user's own paths (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.gemini). Anyone who can control that binary's output already runs code as the user, so crashing the menu-bar app gains them nothing and crosses no trust boundary. (3) The claimed crash on every relaunch is wrong. CachedFetch.swift:34-36 calls decode(data) before cache.writePayload(data), so the process traps before a hostile payload can be written to the DiskCache, and the next launch does not replay it. The finding offers 'hostile or compromised upstream' as a precondition without showing how an attacker gets there. Recommend clamping rem as a hardening fix, not as a vulnerability.
